Depends on agent-53f38d95 (decision trace) landing first so `CostSource` surfacing has a home.","claimed-at":"2026-04-22T22:34:06Z","claimed-machine":"eitri","claimed-pid":"2792459","closing_commit_sha":"9c80eb189c816d60695adf7d64935694548d0264","created_at":"2026-04-22T21:36:22.188965471Z","description":"## Motivation

DDx consumer goal G3: "the selected provider should be the 'best' that meets whatever the requirements are — available, with quota available, **and lowest cost**." Today the routing engine has no cost dimension on `ProviderEntry`; scoring uses only quota + cooldown + perf + locality. When two providers serve the same model with different prices, the engine picks by name or score, not cost.

## Scope

### Data model

Add to `internal/routing.ProviderEntry`:

- `CostUSDPer1kTokens float64` — nil/zero if unknown.
- `CostSource string` — `"catalog" | "subscription" | "unknown" | "user-config"`. Surfaces in decision trace so operators know where the number came from.

Populate at `buildRoutingInputs` time:

- **Endpoint providers (openrouter, lmstudio, omlx, ollama, minimax, qwen, zai, openai):** look up in the existing model catalog (`internal/modelcatalog`) by resolved model ID. When the catalog has a price, use it. When absent, leave zero + `CostSource: "unknown"`.
- **Subscription harnesses (claude, codex, gemini):** compute an **effective** cost as a function of quota utilization:
  - At 0-70% quota used: effective cost = 0 (fixed-cost subscription, near-zero marginal).
  - At 70-90%: effective cost = low (encourage spreading load).
  - At 90-100%: effective cost = high (near-quota demotion).
  - Exact numbers in the bead acceptance; tunable via `ServiceOptions`.
  - `CostSource: "subscription"`.
- **`agent` harness (local via endpoints):** cost = electricity estimate from config (off by default — `CostSource: "unknown"` when not configured). Operators who want to model local cost set `ServiceOptions.LocalCostUSDPer1kTokens`.

### Scoring changes

`internal/routing/score.go`: add cost as a tiebreak dimension **after** eligibility, quota OK, and base score. Order becomes:
1. Eligible
2. Quota OK / healthy
3. Base score (profile policy, cooldowns, perf bias) — unchanged
4. **Cost (lower is better)** — new
5. Locality (local cost-class preferred)
6. Name

For unknown-cost providers (`CostSource: "unknown"`): treat as **neutral** in the cost tiebreak — neither preferred nor demoted, so they don't starve known-cost providers but aren't penalized into last place.

### Unknown-cost policy

A documented rule: when all viable candidates have `CostSource: "unknown"`, the cost tiebreak is skipped and locality/name decide. Test covers this.

## Subscription-quota pricing curve

Default curve (tunable):
- 0-70% used: effective $/1k tokens = 0
- 70-80%: 0.1× the pay-per-token rate for the equivalent model
- 80-90%: 0.3× pay-per-token

[AC text]\n   ...\n\n### Summary\n<1-3 sentences of overall context>\n\n### Findings\n<detailed issues, if any; omit when verdict is APPROVE with no findings>\n```\n\nThe review output can be stored as bead evidence:\n\n```bash\nddx bead evidence add <id> --type review --body <path-to-review.md>\n```\n\n## Quorum review\n\n```bash\nddx agent run --quorum=majority --harnesses=claude,codex,gemini \\\n  --prompt review-prompt.md\n```\n\n`--quorum=<policy>` values:\n\n- `majority` — at least ⌈N/2⌉ harnesses must agree on the verdict.\n- `unanimous` — all harnesses must agree.\n- `any` — pass if any harness APPROVES (rarely useful; adversarial\n  checks should require stronger consensus).\n\nUse quorum when:\n\n- The change is high-stakes (migrations, security surface, API\n  contracts, auth).\n- The review surface is controversial and one harness's opinion\n  isn't enough.\n- You want adversarial pressure against a single-model blindspot\n  (different model families have different failure modes).\n\nThe aggregated output shows each harness's verdict side-by-side plus\nthe aggregate decision. Disagreements are surfaced, not hidden.\n\n## Required evidence format\n\nBoth review kinds share an evidence contract: **no verdict without\nevidence.**\n\n- \"APPROVE\" with no `Evidence:` lines → reject as malformed.\n- \"REQUEST_CHANGES\" without pointing at the change needed → reject.\n- \"BLOCK\" without a reason → reject (see the related bug\n  ddx-39e27896 about `review-malfunction` retries).\n\nEvidence takes one of these forms:\n\n1. **File:line reference**: `cli/internal/bead/store.go:142`\n2. **Test output**: `FAIL: TestBeadClose_UnclaimsOnNonSuccess (0.01s)`\n3. **Diff hunk**: a short quote from the diff showing the offending\n   or approved change.\n4. **Explicit \"not verifiable\"**: the AC is written in a way that\n   cannot be mechanically checked; flag this as a bead-authoring\n   issue rather than silently approving.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Hallucinated approval.** \"Looks good to me!\" with no per-AC\n  grading. The review is worthless.\n- **Reviewing the prompt instead of the diff.** The reviewer evaluated\n  \"what you intended\" not \"what you actually changed.\" Verdict must\n  reference the diff or the resulting code.\n- **Verdict without evidence.** Every verdict must have at least one\n  evidence line; APPROVE is no exception (evidence can be \"AC met:\n  `go test ./foo/... passes` output attached\").\n- **Silencing disagreement in quorum.** If two harnesses disagree,\n  don't collapse to a single \"decision.\" Surface the disagreement\n  in the output and let the human decide.\n- **Quorum for routine work.** Single-harness bead review is fine\n  for most beads. Reserve quorum for the cases that justify the\n  cost.\n\n## Subagents: not this skill's business\n\nSome harnesses can run a quorum in forked/isolated subagent\ncontexts; each harness implements this differently. This skill\ndoesn't specify how isolation is achieved —\n`ddx agent run --quorum=<policy> --harnesses=<list>` is the\nportable invocation, and the harness decides whether to fork,\nspawn, or run inline.\n\n## CLI reference\n\n```bash\n# Bead review (single-reviewer AC grading)\nddx bead review <id>                           # generate review prompt\nddx bead review <id> --execute --harness claude  # dispatch and grade\nddx bead evidence add <id> --type review --body r.md  # store review\n\n# Quorum review (multi-harness)\nddx agent run --quorum=majority \\\n  --harnesses=claude,codex \\\n  --prompt review.md\n\nddx agent run --quorum=unanimous \\\n  --harnesses=claude,codex,gemini \\\n  --prompt review.md\n```\n\nFull flag list: `ddx bead review --help`, `ddx agent run --help`.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

The corpus answers 'are WE getting better' across model, harness, and provider revisions over time.

Direct response to the user's signal: 'as we identify "interesting" bead executions, we should start tracking them so we can make a benchmark out of them. Each should represent some particular capability or failure, which we can then use to track and compare across model, harness, and provider revisions.'

## Scope

### 1. Corpus index + per-bead schema

scripts/beadbench/corpus.yaml — the canonical index:

```yaml
version: 1
beads:
  - id: agent-39f79181
    capability: sampling-resolver-cli-wiring
    promoted: 2026-04-27
    promoted_by: erik
  - id: agent-b6b15fb0
    failure_mode: openai-flavor-thinking-leak
    promoted: 2026-04-26
    promoted_by: erik
```

scripts/beadbench/corpus/<bead-id>.yaml — per-bead detail:

```yaml
bead_id: agent-39f79181
project_root: /Users/erik/Projects/agent
base_rev: ec41a51        # before the change
known_good_rev: 9a8d7fe  # the resolution
captured: 2026-04-27
capability: sampling-resolver-cli-wiring
failure_mode: ''         # populated when promoted BECAUSE of failure
difficulty: easy|medium|hard
prompt_kind: implement-with-spec | port-by-analogy | debug-and-fix | review
notes: free text, what makes this bead instructive
```

Each entry must reference a real closed bead in .ddx/beads.jsonl with reachable base_rev / known_good_rev. Validator at load time.

### 2. /promote-bead curation flow

Manual gate — automated promotion would dilute the corpus.

Slash command (or `ddx bead promote <id>`): after an execution finishes, prompt the operator with:
  - 'this bead surfaced X. Promote to corpus? [y/N]'
  - capability tag (free-form, validated against known tags + warning when introducing a new one)
  - failure_mode tag (free-form, only when the bead surfaced a failure)
  - difficulty
  - notes (one paragraph)

Writes both the corpus.yaml entry and the per-bead detail file. Refuses to promote if the bead is open, has no closing commit, or already exists in the corpus.

### 3. Initial migration

Pass through the last ~20 closed beads on master. Manually identify 3-5 genuinely instructive ones — examples of clear capability demonstrations or notable failure modes. Promote with capability tags. Goal: corpus is non-empty when this lands so the schema is exercised, not aspirational.

Candidates from recent history (illustrative, not authoritative — the migration pass picks them):
- agent-39f79181 (ADR-007 v1 sampling resolver wiring)
- agent-b6b15fb0 (provider-wire thinking-field leak fix)
- agent-37aeb88e (the 2026-04-27 omlx Qwen tool-loop preflight failure)

### 4. Capability taxonomy seed

scripts/beadbench/corpus/capabilities.yaml — controlled vocabulary, additive:

```yaml
- name: sampling-resolver-cli-wiring
  area: cli
  description: ...
- name: openai-flavor-thinking-leak
  area: provider
  description: ...
```

Bead promotions reference these by name. Adding a new capability requires updating this file (= explicit decision, not free-form drift).

### 5. Run-time integration

Manifest arms in scripts/beadbench/manifest-v1.json gain a corpus filter — 'run only beads tagged with capability X' or 'run all corpus beads'. The existing bench runner already accepts task IDs; this just constrains the task set.

## Out of scope (separate beads)

- TerminalBench / SWE-bench / other external-benchmark adapters (sister bead).
- Benchmark-history aggregator (joining runs into a capability × model × harness × provider × revision matrix).
- Per-capability regression detection (alerts when a previously-passing capability fails).

## Why epic

This is curation infrastructure that compounds — every promotion adds value but no single promotion is the whole feature. The schema needs to land, then the slash command, then the migration pass, then the runner integration. hard-pins `DDX_BENCH_DATASET="terminal-bench@2.0"` and the entire benchmark
rig (including subset-v2 selection rules) is keyed to TB-2. Switching to TB-1
just to satisfy the bead literally would invalidate the rest of the harness.

I will not silently substitute a different TB-2 task (e.g. `fix-git`,
`headless-terminal`, `prove-plus-comm`) for the canary because:
  - The AC names a specific task, and substitution risks the next reviewer /
    follow-up bead inheriting an unstated assumption.

    the bead description.

      success to model task-solving ability.

  (C) Author a minimal `hello-world` task inside
      `scripts/benchmark/external/terminal-bench-2-local/` (or similar)
      and point the canary subset at it. This is a larger lift but gives
      a stable trivial-task canary going forward; probably out of scope
      for Step 1.

Option (B) most accurately matches the bead description's stated goal and
is the lowest-cost path. Option (A) is the most direct interpretation if
the AC's `reward=1` wording is load-bearing.

6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.","closing_commit_sha":"5dc25b8d468fb47dc5086e516bcaff9c2da87c27","created_at":"2026-05-06T21:46:16.747791682Z","description":"PROBLEM
A completed Fizeau/DDx run can print a warning after the agent succeeds:

WARN session logger: write error err="write .ddx/agent-logs/svc-1778103547795097343.jsonl: file already closed"

The observed run completed its command_execution, created detached-HEAD commit 50ba08b, and produced a final response. The warning is post-run session-log persistence noise, but it can also mean a late routing-quality override event was not persisted to the per-session JSONL log. That weakens UsageReport/routing-quality reconstruction even though the user-visible execution succeeded.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
service_session_log.go:34 opens the service-owned session logger and service_session_log.go:91 writes terminal session.end events through the same logger. service_execute.go:423 defers final write/close from the runExecute goroutine and service_execute.go:436 closes the logger as soon as runExecute unwinds. service_taillog.go:153 handles final-event fanout and service_taillog.go:163 writes an override event to the same serviceSessionLog from the fanout goroutine immediately before forwarding the final event. That fanout write can race with runExecute closing the logger. internal/session/logger.go:93 closes the underlying file, but internal/session/logger.go:97-100 leaves l.file non-nil, so any late Write reaches internal/session/logger.go:85 and logs "session logger: write error" against a closed file.

PROPOSED FIX
Make service session-log ownership deterministic so all session-log events that belong to an Execute call are persisted before the logger is closed. Prefer moving or synchronizing override-event persistence so the final-event fanout cannot write to a logger after runExecute closes it. Add a defensive logger close behavior only if it complements, rather than hides, the ordering fix: Logger.Close may set l.file nil after close, but the regression test must still prove the override event is persisted, not silently dropped.

In-scope files:
- service_execute.go
- service_taillog.go
- service_session_log.go
- internal/session/logger.go
- focused tests in service_*_test.go and/or internal/session/logger_test.go

NON-SCOPE
Do not change the public Execute event schema, harness-native stream parsers, benchmark matrix reporting, DDx CLI behavior, or TerminalBench/FHI logic. Do not suppress the warning without preserving the late override/routing-quality session-log event.

## Why no code change is being committed

This bead's acceptance criterion ("vidar passes fix-git-style: finds the right approach, completes the task, reward=1") cannot be satisfied by code changes in this execute-bead worktree, and the in-tree fix path that would address the underlying failure mode has already been explicitly rejected. Specifically:

### 1. AC is unsatisfiable from a code worktree

The AC requires running a benchmark task end-to-end against the vidar provider (Qwen3.5-27B-4bit on omlx), observing reward=1, and demonstrating the model "finds the right approach". An execute-bead worktree has no provider access, no omlx runtime, and no benchmark harness wired up to record reward. Verification is empirical, not static.

The AC also names "fix-git-style" while the bead title and description name "cobol-modernization". The two task names appear to have been crossed in templating; whichever is intended, both are benchmark-eval outcomes, not unit-testable code states.

### 2. The natural code fix has been WONTFIX'd

The repository already designed a harness-level fix for exactly this failure mode: `docs/research/tool-call-loop-pivot-2026-05-01.md` (PIVOT-1) proposed replacing the unconditional hard-abort at `internal/core/loop.go:736-744` with a configurable strategy-pivot recovery (inject a redirect message, reset counters, retry up to a limit).

PIVOT-1 was decomposed into three implementation beads, all of which are now CLOSED with status WONTFIX:

- `agent-b05126ab` (PIVOT: Add new types/fields to agent.go) — closed WONTFIX
- `agent-08a538a7` (PIVOT: Implement pivot branch in loop.go) — closed WONTFIX
- `agent-5ef15e17` (PIVOT: Three pivot test cases in loop_test.go) — closed WONTFIX

Common rationale on all three:
> "harness should not contain deterministic loop-recovery logic. The model should self-correct via better system prompt (PRESET beads). PIVOT conflicts with the design principle of minimal harness intervention."

The follow-on benchmark bead (`agent-b2ce8974`, "BENCH: Re-run TB-2 after PIVOT+PRESET") was also closed WONTFIX with "Moving to individual task approach instead of matrix runs. PIVOT+PRESET approach superseded."

Implementing the pivot here would directly contradict that recorded design decision.

### 3. The investigation work for this exact failure is already closed

Sister bead `fizeau-aedbd35d` ("bench/cobol-modernization: sonnet pass, vidar tool-call loop") was a kind:investigation bead opened against the same failure run. It closed APPROVE earlier today (2026-05-03) with reviewer note:
> "Bead has no explicit acceptance criteria and is labeled `kind:investigation`; the diff delivers exactly what an investigation bead should: hypothesis confirmation with file:line citations, token/runtime evidence from both runs, cross-reference to the existing PIVOT-1 design doc, and four scoped follow-ups."

So the diagnostic work this bead's failure motivates is already done and merged at commit 114f6bdc.

## What a follow-up attempt would need

To make `vidar passes <task>` actually achievable as a closable bead, one of the following must happen first:

1. The WONTFIX on PIVOT-2/3/4 is reversed (requires owner sign-off that overrides the "minimal harness intervention" principle), OR
2. The PRESET / system-prompt path produces a vidar build that empirically passes the named task, at which point this bead becomes a verification run rather than a code task, OR
3. The bead is rewritten with an AC that is testable from a code worktree (e.g., "loop.go emits structured `tool_call_loop` telemetry with a fingerprint snippet so post-run analysis can group failures") rather than an end-to-end benchmark outcome.

Until one of those happens, any commit landed under this bead would either re-implement work that was just rejected (option 1 collision) or be unrelated to the AC (option 3 collision).

## What is NOT blocking

- No technical blocker on the loop.go change itself — the design is fully specified in `docs/research/tool-call-loop-pivot-2026-05-01.md` and could be implemented in ~30 minutes if the WONTFIX were reversed.
- No missing investigation — `fizeau-aedbd35d` already cited file:line evidence and token counts.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Run the medium-cost fiz-wrapper TerminalBench comparison.
#
# Defaults:
#   - tier: wide (15 tasks)
#   - reps: 1
#   - jobs: 1
#   - output: benchmark-results/matrix-medium-model-<tier>-<UTC>
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/benchmark/run_medium_model_terminalbench_comparison.sh
#   scripts/benchmark/run_medium_model_terminalbench_comparison.sh canary
#   scripts/benchmark/run_medium_model_terminalbench_comparison.sh wide

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
cd "${ROOT}"

TIER="${1:-wide}"
case "${TIER}" in
  help|-h|--help)
    cat <<'EOF'
usage: scripts/benchmark/run_medium_model_terminalbench_comparison.sh [canary|wide]

Run the official medium-model TerminalBench fiz comparison through one Harbor-installed
FizeauAgent. The wrapper sets the comparison pins internally, so the only manual
environment variable you normally need is OPENROUTER_API_KEY for the fiz OpenRouter lanes.

Single command:
  OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-... scripts/benchmark/run_medium_model_terminalbench_comparison.sh

Use `canary` for the 3-task preflight:
  OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-... scripts/benchmark/run_medium_model_terminalbench_comparison.sh canary

Official lanes:
  fiz-harness-claude-sonnet-4-6
  fiz-harness-codex-gpt-5-4-mini
  fiz-harness-pi-gpt-5-4-mini
  fiz-harness-opencode-gpt-5-4-mini
  fiz-openrouter-claude-sonnet-4-6
  fiz-openrouter-gpt-5-4-mini

Artifacts:
  benchmark-results/matrix-medium-model-<tier>-<UTC>/matrix.json
  benchmark-results/matrix-medium-model-<tier>-<UTC>/matrix.md
  benchmark-results/matrix-medium-model-<tier>-<UTC>/costs.json

Invalid cells:
  invalid_quota, invalid_auth, invalid_setup, and invalid_provider are recorded in matrix.md
  with their cause and log path. They are excluded from mean reward and denominator handling.

Raw Harbor Claude/Codex/pi/opencode adapters remain diagnostics only.
EOF
    exit 0
    ;;
  canary|wide) ;;
  *)
    echo "usage: $0 [canary|wide]" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

if [[ -z "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}" ]]; then
  echo "missing OPENROUTER_API_KEY; required for fiz OpenRouter comparison cells" >&2
  exit 1
fi

OUT="benchmark-results/matrix-medium-model-${TIER}-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
RUNNER="scripts/benchmark/run_vidar_qwen36_terminalbench_baseline.sh"
OFFICIAL_PROFILES=(
  fiz-harness-claude-sonnet-4-6
  fiz-harness-codex-gpt-5-4-mini
  fiz-harness-pi-gpt-5-4-mini
  fiz-harness-opencode-gpt-5-4-mini
  fiz-openrouter-claude-sonnet-4-6
  fiz-openrouter-gpt-5-4-mini
)
OFFICIAL_PROFILES_CSV="$(IFS=,; echo "${OFFICIAL_PROFILES[*]}")"

common_env=(
  "TIER=${TIER}"
  "REPS=1"
  "JOBS=1"
  "FORCE_RERUN=1"
  "HARBOR_FORCE_BUILD=${HARBOR_FORCE_BUILD:-1}"
  "OUT=${OUT}"
)

echo "Running medium-cost TerminalBench comparison"
echo "  tier: ${TIER}"
echo "  out:  ${OUT}"
echo

echo "1/1 fiz wrapper lanes via Harbor"
env \
  "${common_env[@]}" \
  BASELINE=local \
  HARNESSES=fiz \
  PROFILE="${OFFICIAL_PROFILES_CSV}" \
  "${RUNNER}"

echo
echo "Comparison complete:"
echo "  ${OUT}/matrix.json"
echo "  ${OUT}/matrix.md"
echo "  ${OUT}/costs.json"

### Medium-model fiz-wrapper comparison

Use the dedicated entrypoint for the medium-cost fiz-wrapper comparison:

```bash
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-... \
  scripts/benchmark/run_medium_model_terminalbench_comparison.sh
```

That single command is the official comparison entrypoint. The wrapper sets
`TIER=wide`, `REPS=1`, `JOBS=1`, `FORCE_RERUN=1`, `HARBOR_FORCE_BUILD=1`, and
`HARNESSES=fiz` internally, then runs one Harbor-installed `FizeauAgent`
against the official profile CSV. To do only the 3-task preflight:

```bash
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-... \
  scripts/benchmark/run_medium_model_terminalbench_comparison.sh canary
```

Cells included in the official comparison:

- `fiz-harness-claude-sonnet-4-6`
- `fiz-harness-codex-gpt-5-4-mini`
- `fiz-harness-pi-gpt-5-4-mini`
- `fiz-harness-opencode-gpt-5-4-mini`
- `fiz-openrouter-claude-sonnet-4-6`
- `fiz-openrouter-gpt-5-4-mini`

The raw Harbor Claude/Codex/pi/opencode adapters remain diagnostics only. The
official claims use the six `fiz-*` lanes routed through `FizeauAgent`, not the
native Harbor adapter rows.

Artifacts are written under
`benchmark-results/matrix-medium-model-<tier>-<UTC>/`:

- `matrix.json`
- `matrix.md`
- `costs.json`
- per-cell logs under `*/logs/agent/`

Invalid cells are classified as `invalid_quota`, `invalid_auth`,
`invalid_setup`, or `invalid_provider`. They stay visible in `matrix.md` with
their cause and log path, but they are excluded from mean reward and
denominator handling when the matrix is aggregated.

### Bootstrap Subset Selection

`TIER=wide` should not rely on a hand-maintained sense of task difficulty. Use
the selector below to bootstrap a 15-task subset from public
Terminal-Bench-2 leaderboard trial rewards:

```bash
scripts/benchmark/select_terminalbench_subset.py
```

The selector reads reward files from
`harborframework/terminal-bench-2-leaderboard` on Hugging Face, groups
submissions into broad `frontier`, `medium_frontier`, and `non_frontier`
families by Fizeau catalog power, and emits:

- tasks almost everyone passes
- tasks almost nobody passes
- tasks mostly passed by frontier submissions
- tasks mostly passed by medium-frontier submissions
- tasks consistently passed by non-frontier submissions
- probes where the monotonic difficulty assumption appears false

The generated manifest is written to
`scripts/beadbench/external/termbench-subset-external-bootstrap.json`. Review
the monotonicity report before replacing the committed `wide` subset.

Submission directories are interpreted as `Harness__Model` when that delimiter
is present. The `Model` field is matched against
`internal/modelcatalog/catalog/models.yaml` first, using the same broad display
variant behavior as catalog model eligibility. Leaderboard-only models that are
not yet in the catalog are assigned bootstrap powers in
`scripts/benchmark/terminalbench_model_power.json`; exact submission-name
overrides use a `submission:` prefix for rows that do not expose a clean
`Harness__Model` split or represent a multi-model stack.

### Benchmark Evidence

Benchmark runner outputs are benchmark-specific, but long-term model power
should be derived from normalized raw evidence keyed by model, harness,
provider, and benchmark. New importers should project source reports into the
schema at `scripts/benchmark/benchmark-evidence.schema.json`; see
`docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-012-benchmark-evidence-ledger.md`.
The relevant command surface is `go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-terminalbench`,
`go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-beadbench`, `go run ./cmd/bench evidence
import-external`, `go run ./cmd/bench evidence append`, and `go run ./cmd/bench
fhi delta|rank`.

Curated external snapshots can be imported with:

```bash
go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-external \
  --source cmd/bench/testdata/external-benchmarks/rapid-mlx-mhi.md \
  --out /tmp/rapid-mlx.jsonl
```

The same command accepts SkillsBench CSV, SWE-bench CSV, and HumanEval JSONL
fixtures. Imported rows keep `unknown` harness/provider values explicit instead
of dropping them, and HumanEval rows are flagged as low-cost model-power
evidence rather than primary FHI coverage.

### Claude and Codex reference baselines

Set `BASELINE=frontier` to run native Claude Code and Codex reference cells:

```bash
BASELINE=frontier TIER=canary REPS=1 FORCE_RERUN=1 JOBS=1 \
  scripts/benchmark/run_vidar_qwen36_terminalbench_baseline.sh
```

These cells are **not model-controlled comparisons** against Vidar/Qwen. They
answer a different question: how the native subscription/reference harnesses
perform on the same TerminalBench tasks. Keep them in a separate table from the
local-model rows unless the analysis explicitly calls out the model confound.

The runner uses paired one-cell invocations so Claude Code only runs with
`claude-native-sonnet-4-6` (`sonnet-4.6`) and Codex only runs with
`codex-native-gpt-5-4-mini` (`gpt-5.4-mini`). This avoids meaningless
cross-products like Claude Code with the Codex profile.

Prepare linux artifacts before running inside Harbor containers:

```bash
scripts/benchmark/run_medium_model_terminalbench_comparison.sh canary
```

The runner prepares native Claude/Codex harness artifacts automatically. Harbor
Docker jobs are assumed to run on the host architecture by default, so the
runner builds `fiz` for the host `GOARCH`, looks for native CLI artifacts under
`benchmark-results/bin/claude-linux-<goarch>/claude` and
`benchmark-results/bin/codex-linux-<goarch>/codex`, and otherwise uses the
locally installed `claude` / `codex` binaries when they match the container
architecture. If a non-native container platform is forced, set
`HARBOR_NODE_ARCH=x64` or `HARBOR_NODE_ARCH=arm64` and the runner will instead
`npm pack` the matching CLI packages, upload the corresponding Node.js tarball,
and install the CLIs inside the Harbor container. If API key environment
variables are not present, it also packages local `~/.claude` and `~/.codex`
auth/config state into gitignored tarballs under
`benchmark-results/bin/native-homes/` so the container can use the same logged-in
CLI accounts. Set `HARBOR_SKIP_NATIVE_HOME=1` to disable that behavior.

Manual overrides remain available:

```bash
HARBOR_CLAUDE_ARTIFACT=/path/to/claude \
HARBOR_CODEX_ARTIFACT=/path/to/codex \
  scripts/benchmark/run_medium_model_terminalbench_comparison.sh canary
```

Authentication can use API keys passed by the profile env vars
(`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`) or a tarred harness home directory:

```bash
tar -C "$HOME" -czf benchmark-results/bin/claude-home.tgz .claude
tar -C "$HOME" -czf benchmark-results/bin/codex-home.tgz .codex

HARBOR_CLAUDE_HOME_TARBALL=benchmark-results/bin/claude-home.tgz \
HARBOR_CODEX_HOME_TARBALL=benchmark-results/bin/codex-home.tgz \
BASELINE=frontier TIER=canary REPS=1 FORCE_RERUN=1 JOBS=1 \
  scripts/benchmark/run_vidar_qwen36_terminalbench_baseline.sh
```

Do not commit those tarballs or benchmark-result artifacts.

To compare `fiz` against the same medium-cost model families through
OpenRouter, run separate `fiz` cells with the official OpenRouter profiles:

```bash
TIER=canary HARNESSES=fiz PROFILE=fiz-openrouter-gpt-5-4-mini REPS=1 FORCE_RERUN=1 JOBS=1 \
  scripts/benchmark/run_vidar_qwen36_terminalbench_baseline.sh

TIER=canary HARNESSES=fiz PROFILE=fiz-openrouter-claude-sonnet-4-6 REPS=1 FORCE_RERUN=1 JOBS=1 \
  scripts/benchmark/run_vidar_qwen36_terminalbench_baseline.sh
